main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling salted fish in the shared kitchen; settled on weekends only, with a heads-up to B and C moving laundry to weekend mornings.

A-B.evidence: A and B never address each other; both end up accepting D's weekend cooking arrangement (turns 7, 9, 11).

A-C.evidence: A and C never speak to each other; both complain about the smell and C ends up accepting the weekend plan (turns 3, 19).

A-D.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (turn 5 weekend suggestion); D agrees to weekends (turn 6); A: 'that works for me' (turn 7); D cites the deal with A (turns 15, 18).

B-C.evidence: B and C never address each other; both accept the weekend arrangement with their own accommodations (turns 11, 19).

B-D.evidence: B asks for a heads-up (turn 9); D: 'sure, I can let you know' (turn 10); B: 'That works for me' (turn 11); D repeats the promise (turn 27).

C-D.evidence: C rejects the weekend plan and asks for non-laundry nights (turn 14); D refuses and offers weekend-morning laundry (turn 15); C: 'That works' (turn 19).
